subject.title: Bounded memory tool with hard character limits

question: Should OpenClaw define a first-class bounded memory write/CRUD contract in the default memory slot, and what hard-limit, identity, replacement, duplicate/consolidation, snapshot, config, and secret-handling semantics should it expose?
rationale: The requested behavior creates a new public memory-writing and possibly configurable persistence contract with security-sensitive handling of durable user data, so implementation cannot be safely selected by automation alone.

options.title: Define default bounded memory CRUD
options.body: Approve a memory-core/default memory contract and implement add/list/replace/remove with hard limits, stable block identity, safety checks, and docs/tests.

options.title: Prototype outside default memory
options.body: Route the work through an optional plugin or ClawHub-style experiment until the API and safety model are proven enough for the default memory slot.

options.title: Keep default memory read-only for now
options.body: Limit near-term core work to diagnostics and narrow flush bounds while leaving general memory writes to optional plugins.

recommendation.title: Define default bounded memory CRUD
recommendation.body: Approve a memory-core/default memory contract and implement add/list/replace/remove with hard limits, stable block identity, safety checks, and docs/tests.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a cross-cutting product/API/security choice for the default memory surface, and CONTRIBUTING identifies steipete as the final product decision owner.
